title: pkgx pantry package.yml
description: Schema for a pantry package.yml recipe, derived from libpkgx's parser. Reused by go-zpkg/zpkb to validate recipes (YAML and its HCL2 front-end). CLOSED at the root and in build, test, distributable and versions: an unknown key there is refused rather than ignored, because a key nothing implements used to validate and be dropped, which reads to anyone opening the recipe as a feature they have. Those five containers are closed because they were surveyed (schema/corpuskeys_test.go, ZPKB_RECIPES_CORPUS); scriptStep, fixture, runtime and interprets are deliberately still open, not because they should be but because nobody has measured them yet. The object form of `provides` and the dep/env maps stay open by nature: their keys are project and platform names, not a fixed set.

members.description: A SET: the packages this recipe names, as project -> version constraint. A recipe with members describes a tree rather than one package, and must not also carry a distributable.

distributable.description: Where the source is fetched from (null when the package has no sources).

sources.description: ADDITIONAL artifacts the build needs — a second tarball, a patch, a signature — as a list in which EVERY entry is fetched and pinned. Not the list form of `distributable`, which is fallback MIRRORS of one source (the first that answers wins). Each entry needs a sha256; a digest mismatch fails the build. Archives are unpacked into `dest`, plain files (`extract: false`) are copied there.

versions.description: How available versions are discovered: an explicit list, a single source object, or an array of source objects (multiple sources).

build.description: The build. A string/array is script shorthand; an object carries dependencies/env/etc.

skip.description: fix-up steps to skip: fix-machos, fix-patchelf, libtool-cleanup, flatten-includes

test.description: Post-build sanity test run in a fresh sandbox.

provides.description: Programs/paths this package provides, eg. bin/foo. Platform-keyable.

runtime.description: environment exported to consumers at runtime

platforms.description: platforms this package builds for: darwin, linux, windows, or <os>/<arch>

provenance.description: where this recipe's build came from: the files of the PROJECT ITSELF that were read to write it. No other packaging system records this, and ours must, because the recipes are written rather than converted — pkgxdev/pantry carries no licence, so it cannot seed ours (go-zpkg/packages#431). This is what makes "ours" checkable instead of asserted: `read` names the project's own configure, CMakeLists.txt, Makefile, INSTALL or README, and `note` says in one line what they said to do. It is enumerated here so it is no longer accepted and silently dropped; `zpkb lint --require-provenance` is what makes it mandatory, per tree, because an upstream recipe has no reason to carry it.

read.description: paths inside the project's own source that the build was derived from; at least one

consulted.description: other distributions' packaging of the same project that was read while writing this recipe — Nix, Guix, Spack, Homebrew, pkgx, Debian, Fedora. Reading them is bibliography: their packaging is where the hard-won FACTS live (which configure flag a project needs on darwin, which dependency it does not declare, which test hangs under qemu), and a fact has no author. Writing the recipes rather than converting them (go-zpkg/packages#431) is about EXPRESSION — we take nobody's script. This list is a citation list, not a confession, and it is what makes the distinction auditable: `read` is what the build DERIVES from, `consulted` is what was learned from.

note.description: one line on what those files said to do

npm.description: an npm package name, scoped or not. Resolved by versions.Resolve and used as the vulnerability identity (versions/identity.go). Enumerated here because the code has always honoured it and this schema did not say so; 21 recipes of the upstream corpus use it.

url.description: a URL to scrape versions from

match.description: regex selecting version strings from the URL body

sha.description: where the expected SHA-256 of the archive is published, usually ${{url}}.sha256 — the build fetches it and refuses a mismatch (build/runner.go, ErrChecksumMismatch). It is served by the same host as the archive in every recipe that uses it, so it catches corruption, not substitution; fetch.Pin's trust-on-first-use is the control for the latter. Enumerated here because the runner has always honoured it and this schema did not say so.

sha256.description: the digest PINNED IN THE RECIPE, by whoever read the release. Unlike `sha` it needs no network and is not served by the host it vouches for, and unlike fetch.Pin's trust-on-first-use it can refuse a FIRST fetch — the case neither of the others covers. Keyed by version, because the url interpolates {{version.raw}} and one entry serves every version the recipe resolves: a scalar is right for exactly one of them. The scalar form is allowed only for a recipe that resolves a single version. A recipe that pins is fail-closed: building a version absent from the map is refused, not fetched unverified.

strip-components.description: leading path components to strip on extract

extract.description: false COPIES the URL as one plain file instead of unpacking an archive (a .pem, a .patch). Asked for, never inferred from an unknown extension, so a misspelt archive suffix still fails loudly. Requires sha256; refuses strip-components and ref.

sourceObject.description: One entry of `sources`. Closed: a key nothing implements is refused.

strip-components.description: leading path components to strip when an archive is unpacked; refused with extract: false

dest.description: directory, relative to the build directory, the entry lands in (default: the build directory itself). A plain file keeps the last segment of the URL's path as its name, and never overwrites a file already there.

extract.description: false COPIES the URL as one plain file instead of unpacking an archive. Default true.

constraint.description: a semver constraint (*, ^1, ~1.2, >=1, =1.2.3), boolean, number, or null shorthand

depMap.description: project → constraint, optionally nested under a platform key (darwin|linux|windows[/arch] or <arch>) OR under a VERSION SCOPE — a semver predicate on the version of THIS package, such as `<18` or `>=3<3.12`, whose sub-map applies only to the versions satisfying it. ⛔ WHY A VERSION SCOPE EXISTS: a recipe resolves many versions and used to state one dependency block, so every bound had to satisfy all of them — in practice the most restrictive requirement of the OLDEST resolvable version, which the newest then paid for forever. Measured (go-zpkg/zpkb#488): llvm.org's `cmake.org: '>=3<3.29'` excluded 69 of cmake's 71 versions, and its `python.org: '>=3<3.12'` excluded 50 of python's although LLVM 23.1.5's own llvm/CMakeLists.txt:1102-1111 sets LLVM_MINIMUM_PYTHON_VERSION 3.8 with NO ceiling — the bound belonged to a distutils-era llvm and there was no way to say so. ⭐ WHY A PREDICATE IS UNAMBIGUOUS HERE: depKey admits only [A-Za-z0-9._+-] segments, so a key holding any of < > = ^ ~ * cannot be a project or a platform; the discriminator is this schema's own grammar rather than a second one. ⚠ A bare `5.40` IS a legal depKey and therefore reads as a PROJECT — a scope must carry an operator, so write `=5.40`. ⛔ RESOLUTION ORDER, because one project may appear in more than one place: plain keys first, then platform, then version scope, each overriding the previous (build.reduceDepMap). A reduction that does not know the package's version — `closure`, `catalog`, `depgaps`, `spechash` all walk the pantry before anything is resolved — UNIONS the scopes and lets the stricter constraint win, because a closure that over-constrains fails loudly at resolution while one that under-constrains ships an artifact linked against something the recipe never asked for.

depMapKey.description: a TOP-LEVEL key of a dependency map: a depKey (project or platform) or a version scope. ⛔ Only at the top level: a SUB-map's keys are projects, so the nested propertyNames stays depKey — a scope inside a scope would be a second question about the same version and nothing reduces it.

versionScopeKey.description: a semver predicate scoping a dependency sub-map to the versions of THIS package that satisfy it: `<18`, `>=3<3.12`, `^2`, `~3.5`, `=5.40`. It MUST contain at least one of < > = ^ ~ * — that is what makes it distinguishable from a depKey, whose charset excludes all six, and it is why a bare `5.40` is read as a project name instead. The grammar is the same one `if:` conditions already use on script steps (buildscript.matchGuard), so a recipe has one way to say "at these versions" rather than two.

depKey.description: a key of a dependency map: a project name (gnu.org/gcc, crates.io/semverator) or a platform key (linux, darwin/aarch64, x86-64). Slash-separated segments of [A-Za-z0-9._+-], each holding at least one character that is not a dot — so `.` and `..` are not segments. A key here becomes a registry repository and a store path by concatenation, which is why its shape is constrained at the authoritative schema rather than wherever it is used. Measured against the upstream pantry: 1929 recipes, 7410 keys at both levels, every one accepted.

envMap.description: KEY → value(s); a platform key (darwin|linux|windows[/arch] or <arch>) nests a sub-map merged/overridden for that target

if.description: guard: a platform, arch, <os>/<arch>, or semver range — evaluated against the build TARGET
